content.user_title: Plan Fitness Email Campaigns and Membership Journeys
content.value_statement: Fitness campaigns can misuse sensitive information, outdated membership records, or unclear promotional permissions. This skill guides campaign copy, audience rules, and membership journeys using verified facts and consent safeguards.
actual_capabilities: Draft subject lines, preheaders, concise email bodies, and primary calls to action for fitness campaigns.
Define audience segments using declared activity interests, location, trial status, and verified membership or booking state.
Specify journey entry events, delays, branches, exits, re-entry rules, overlap handling, and retry safeguards.
Review campaigns for sensitive-health targeting, unsupported claims, consent gaps, and unclear membership terms.
Plan measurement using trial bookings, first-class attendance, paid conversions, and comparable membership cohorts.
Assess whether a trial-interest form addresses a verified acquisition gap while preserving booking and membership system authority.
limitations: Provides instructions and drafts, not a standalone email delivery service or verified platform integration.
Does not authorize sending, scheduling, personal-data uploads, or changes to live systems.
Does not provide medical advice, legal certification, or health-based eligibility decisions.
Requires current business data, verified offer terms, and platform documentation before implementation or launch.

use_cases.title: Introduce a Beginner Class
use_cases.description: Prepare a welcoming class email with verified availability, clear trial terms, and a single booking call to action.

use_cases.title: Design Trial Nurture
use_cases.description: Map follow-up from trial interest to membership activation, with eligibility checks, exits, and event deduplication.

use_cases.title: Review Membership Campaigns
use_cases.description: Identify targeting risks, stale attendance records, frozen memberships, and missing launch approvals before client delivery.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Class Introduction
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a beginner-class email for [studio] using [verified class details] and [booking URL]. Include a subject, preheader, body, and one CTA. Use placeholders for missing facts and avoid health promises.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Create a single campaign draft.

prompt_templates.title: Define a Trial Audience
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan audience rules for [trial offer] using [declared interests], [locations], and [verified membership states]. Separate promotional permission from interest. List exclusions, missing-data blockers, and assumptions without uploading data.

prompt_templates.title: Map a Membership Journey
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a trial-to-membership journey in [selected platform] using [verified events and consent rules]. Specify entry, data authority, timezone, delays, branches, exits, re-entry, overlap, and deduplication. Include timeout reconciliation and checks before each promotional step. Do not implement or launch.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Plan automation behavior and failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Campaign Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [campaign plan] using [offer terms], [data freshness], [audience rules], and [measurement plan]. Test full classes, frozen memberships, stale attendance, injury replies, youth inquiries, and recurring charges. Prioritize blockers, distinguish facts from assumptions, and identify the next authorized action. Do not send or change records.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Review safety, measurement, and launch readiness.

output_examples.input: Draft a beginner strength-class email for Riverside Studio with a verified Tuesday 6 p.m. session and no approved trial price.
output: Subject: Explore beginner strength at Riverside Studio
Preheader: View the Tuesday 6 p.m. session.
Body: Interested in a beginner strength class? Explore our Tuesday 6 p.m. session and review current availability before booking.
Draft note: Add the verified booking link; omit trial pricing until approved.

output_examples.input: Review a win-back proposal targeting injury tags, promising guaranteed weight loss, and using month-old attendance records.
output: Remove injury-based promotional targeting and the guaranteed weight-loss claim.
Hold attendance-dependent targeting until records are refreshed.
Check current membership state and promotional eligibility; exclude or tailor frozen memberships.
Prepare a neutral class-interest draft without sending or changing customer records.

output_examples.input: Plan trial follow-up when booking confirmation times out and membership activation can occur during the delay.
output: Use the booking system as the authority for confirmed reservations.
Reconcile booking status and logs before retrying a timed-out action; hold the action if uncertainty remains.
Deduplicate repeated business events and preserve provider-supported idempotency.
Exit acquisition nurture after verified membership activation and recheck consent before each promotional message.

best_practices: Provide verified offer terms, booking authority, current membership states, and consent rules before requesting a campaign plan.
Keep health screening separate from marketing data and use declared interests for promotional personalization.
Review live audience counts, exclusions, destinations, timing, and authorization before any send or system change.
anti_patterns: Segmenting promotional audiences by injuries, diagnoses, body size, or inferred health vulnerability.
Treating a draft request, missing consent, or a trial-interest form as permission to send or confirm a booking.
Retrying uncertain actions automatically or measuring success through unsupported health claims and unmatched attribution windows.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does the skill send emails or access my accounts?
faq.answer: No account access is required for planning and drafts. Sending, scheduling, uploads, and live changes require applicable authorization and platform access.

faq.question: Must I use Poptin?
faq.answer: No. The skill preserves your selected platform and considers Poptin only for a relevant, verified acquisition gap.

faq.question: Can injury information drive promotional segments?
faq.answer: No. The skill separates sensitive health intake from marketing and uses declared activity interests and verified business status.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide class details, verified offer terms, booking and membership authorities, audience eligibility, capacity, and the desired next action.

faq.question: How does it handle uncertain bookings or outdated data?
faq.answer: It holds data-dependent targeting until records are refreshed and requires status reconciliation before retrying uncertain actions.
